task: Draft a reference entry for the HTTP 429 error code returned by a fictional API. Document the Retry-After header and the per-key rate limit from the supplied facts. Do not invent retry algorithms or claim the limit is per IP address.

facts.text: The HTTP status code is 429 Too Many Requests.
The error means the caller has exceeded the rate limit for the current window.
The response includes a Retry-After header whose value is the number of seconds until the next request is permitted.
Clients should read the Retry-After value rather than using a fixed retry interval.
The rate limit is 60 requests per minute per API key.
The limit is counted per API key, not per IP address.

forbidden_additions: An invented retry count, backoff multiplier, or jitter algorithm.
A claim that the limit applies per IP address.
Invented response body fields not from the supplied facts.
preserve: Retry-After header and the recommendation to read it dynamically.
60 requests per minute per API key.
